practices.practice: Read the MongoDB-style connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and do not hard-code, log, or commit it; publish a .env.example with placeholders instead.
practices.prior_belief: Read the MongoDB-style connection string from the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable and never hard-code, log, or commit it; use a .env.example with a placeholder.

practices.practice: Always require TLS on the wire (e.g., tls=true or equivalent driver option) and validate server certificates when connecting to an Azure DocumentDB cluster.
practices.prior_belief: Always enable TLS/SSL on the MongoDB client (tls=True / ssl=True) and validate server certificates when connecting to the DocumentDB cluster.

practices.practice: Store connection strings and other secrets in a managed secret store (e.g., Azure Key Vault) or inject them as environment-only values rather than embedding them in code or repository files.
practices.prior_belief: Use a managed secret store (Azure Key Vault) or an environment-only secret mechanism for the connection string and API keys rather than embedding them in code or repository files.

practices.how_found: Azure Key Vault store connection strings best practices

practices.practice: Create a single MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it rather than creating a new client per request; configure pool parameters only after understanding app concurrency patterns.

Tune connection-pool and timeout settings to match your runtime (serverless vs long-running servers vs OLAP) and initialize the client outside the request/handler scope to enable reuse (serverless: small maxPoolSize, short maxIdleTimeMS).
Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network or rate-limit errors and make aggregation/write operations idempotent or detect duplicates to avoid double-counting.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network and server errors; make aggregation and write operations idempotent or detect duplicate execution to avoid double-counting.

practices.practice: Perform numeric aggregations server-side using the aggregation pipeline (db.collection.aggregate with $group and accumulators) rather than fetching documents and summing client-side to reduce network and I/O cost.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side aggregation (MongoDB aggregate pipelines) to compute risk-weighted sums rather than fetching all documents and summing client-side to reduce data transfer and RU/IO consumption.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB aggregation pipeline guidance (learn.microsoft.com) / aggregate command docs

practices.practice: Order aggregation pipeline stages to filter early: place $match first, then $project to keep only required numeric fields, then $group to minimize documents and memory use; verify plan/index usage with explain("executionStats").
practices.prior_belief: When aggregating sums, $match as the first stage, then $project to include only numeric fields required for sum/group to minimize network and memory use; verify with explain() that the index is used.

practices.practice: Use explain("executionStats") and server-side profiling / slow-query logs to confirm index usage and detect COLLSCANs; tune indexes or pipeline ordering when keysExamined/docsExamined indicate inefficiency.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() and server-side profiling to check aggregation plans and index usage and adjust indexes or pipeline ordering if the explain shows collection scans or excessive memory usage.

practices.practice: Store monetary and regulatory numeric values using Decimal128 (or other fixed-point/decimal types) and use aggregation operators like $toDecimal / $convert when needed to avoid floating-point rounding errors.
practices.prior_belief: Use Decimal128 (or a fixed-point numeric type) for storing monetary and regulatory values (risk-weighted assets, CET1 amounts) to avoid floating-point rounding errors.

practices.practice: Create indexes that support the aggregation pipeline (equality fields first, then sort/range) — prefer one well-shaped compound index over many single-field indexes and keep a modest per-collection index budget.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes supporting the aggregation pipeline: add compound indexes on fields used in $match and $group (e.g., account_id, risk_type, report_date) so the pipeline filters early and scans fewer documents.

practices.practice: Prefer DocumentDB's search path: create search indexes with createSearchIndexes and query with $search (textSearch / BM25) rather than relying on the community $text index.

When using vector search, store vectors in a dedicated numeric array field, normalize embeddings for cosine similarity, and create a provider-specific cosmosSearch vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with tuned parameters (dimensions, lBuild/lSearch, maxDegree, efConstruction/efSearch).
practices.prior_belief: If using vector search, store vectors in a dedicated field and create the provider-specific approximate nearest neighbor index (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with tuned parameters (e.g., efConstruction, M, ef) appropriate for recall/latency; normalize vectors before indexing/searching.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search DiskANN HNSW IVF guidance (learn.microsoft.com) / integrated vector store

practices.practice: Limit vector index dimensionality and cardinality and use product quantization or half-precision (fp16) when appropriate to reduce memory and build cost and keep index performance predictable.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the dimensionality and cardinality of vector fields and avoid unbounded growth of vector-indexed collections to keep index build and query cost predictable.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search guidance (learn.microsoft.com) / integrated vector store

practices.practice: Shard only when a collection's storage or throughput exceeds a single physical shard's budget; choose a shard key that matches the most common read filter for read-heavy workloads or the highest-cardinality evenly-distributed field for write-heavy workloads to avoid hot partitions.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a sharding / partition key with high cardinality and that is present in common queries (e.g., account_id or client_id) to avoid hot partitions if the cluster is sharded or provisioned with partitioning.

practices.practice: Seed sample data idempotently (use upserts or bulk_write upserts) and, for ephemeral test data, consider TTL indexes so repeated runs do not accumulate test artifacts.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding sample data, use upserts or idempotent insert patterns and include a short TTL index for ephemeral test documents so repeated runs do not accumulate test artifacts.

practices.practice: Avoid sending raw PII or sensitive balance-level data to external LLM services; minimize exposure by sending de-identified aggregates or running LLMs in an approved, private environment.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid sending raw PII or sensitive balance-level data to external LLMs; send only aggregated, de-identified metrics and ensure the LLM path is disabled or mocked when OPENAI_API_KEY is missing.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB LLM PII guidance", "Azure DocumentDB privacy LLM"

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and collect slow-query logs and cluster metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connection saturation) into Log Analytics; create alerts for throttling, slow queries, and resource saturation.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor cluster-level metrics (CPU, I/O, RU/s or equivalent), set alerts for throttle/slow queries, and instrument the app to capture query latency and aggregation cost to detect regressions early.

practices.practice: Prefer least-privilege credentials (Azure Entra ID / RBAC or per-app users) rather than a single full-access account key; rotate and revoke credentials used for test runs.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer per-collection or per-database least-privilege credentials rather than a single account key with full access; rotate credentials regularly and revoke keys used in test runs.

practices.practice: Compute numerators and denominators together on the server (single aggregation pipeline or transaction where supported) to avoid inconsistent snapshots across multiple client queries; when multi-document transactions aren't available (sharded collections) prefer single-pipeline aggregations.
practices.prior_belief: When presenting computed Basel III ratios, compute numerators and denominators atomically in a single aggregation pipeline stage where possible to avoid inconsistent snapshots across multiple queries.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB aggregation / transaction docs; search: "Azure DocumentDB aggregate atomic snapshot"
